paper.title: Artificial Intelligence in Heritage Tourism: Innovation, Accessibility, and Sustainability in the Digital Age
paper.tldr: It is argued that AI, when implemented in accordance with principles of responsibility, sustainability, and cultural sensitivity, can serve as a strategic instrument for ensuring the accessibility, representativeness, and social relevance of cultural heritage in the digital age.

paper.title: Digitalizing cultural heritage through metaverse applications: challenges, opportunities, and strategies
paper.tldr: The current study aims to explore the potential of metaverse applications in digitalizing cultural heritage, encompassing virtual reconstructions, educational outreach, global accessibility, and sustainability, and evaluates the impact of metaverse applications on public engagement and cultural education.

paper.title: When “Old” Meets “New”: Unlocking the Future of Innovative Technology Implementation in Heritage Tourism
paper.tldr: This paper aims to gain insights into how heritage destinations have adopted innovative technologies into their daily operations, and to reveal future research directions that can guide technology studies in the heritage tourism domain.

OmniLatent: Unified Latent for 3D Part Modeling
paper.tldr: OmniLatent is presented, a unified latent modeling framework for 3D part decomposition that produces semantically meaningful part segmentations with precise boundaries, supports interactive part editing, and completes partial part observations while preserving global object consistency.

paper.title: Structured 3D Latents for Scalable and Versatile 3D Generation
paper.tldr: A novel 3D generation method for versatile and high-quality 3D asset creation by integrating a sparsely-populated 3D grid with dense multiview visual features extracted from a powerful vision foundation model, comprehensively capturing both structural and textural information while maintaining flexibility during decoding.

paper.title: Native and Compact Structured Latents for 3D Generation
paper.tldr: A new sparse voxel structure called O-Voxel, an omni-voxel representation that encodes both geometry and appearance that can robustly model arbitrary topology, and a Sparse Compression VAE which provides a high spatial compression rate and a compact latent space.

paper.title: PartCrafter: Structured 3D Mesh Generation via Compositional Latent Diffusion Transformers
paper.tldr: PartCrafter is introduced, the first structured 3D generative model that jointly synthesizes multiple semantically meaningful and geometrically distinct 3D meshes from a single RGB image, and introduces a compositional latent space, where each 3D part is represented by a set of disentangled latent tokens.

Cosmos Policy: Fine-Tuning Video Models for Visuomotor Control and Planning
paper.tldr: Cosmos Policy is introduced, a simple approach for adapting a large pretrained video model (Cosmos-Predict2) into an effective robot policy through a single stage of post-training on the robot demonstration data collected on the target platform, with no architectural modifications.

paper.title: Wan: Open and Advanced Large-Scale Video Generative Models
paper.tldr: This report presents Wan, a comprehensive and open suite of video foundation models designed to push the boundaries of video generation, built upon the mainstream diffusion transformer paradigm, which consistently outperforms the existing open-source models as well as state-of-the-art commercial solutions across multiple internal and external benchmarks.

paper.title: Fine-Tuning Vision-Language-Action Models: Optimizing Speed and Success
paper.tldr: This work proposes an Optimized Fine-Tuning (OFT) recipe, an instantiation of this recipe, which sets a new state of the art on the LIBERO simulation benchmark, significantly boosting OpenVLA's average success rate across four task suites from 76.5% to 97.1% while increasing action generation throughput by 26$\times$.

paper.title: UniVLA: Learning to Act Anywhere with Task-centric Latent Actions
paper.tldr: This work proposes UniVLA, a new framework for learning cross-embodiment vision-language-action (VLA) policies that achieves superior performance over OpenVLA with less than 1/20 of pretraining compute and 1/10 of downstream data.
